tools.description: Run a PowerShell command in the current working directory (via C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.EXE). PREFER THIS OVER bash ON WINDOWS: bash falls through to cmd.exe here, which has no sleep, no grep, no sed, and breaks on input redirection. Native exit codes are preserved exactly; a failing cmdlet reports 1. Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message. A call still running after 30 seconds is moved to the background automatically (same delivery) — pass a timeout long enough for the work; it still applies to a backgrounded call.
tools.name: powershell
tools.summary: Execute a child process or shell command

tools.description: Execute a shell command in the current working directory (bash on Unix; a real bash (C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe) on Windows: sleep, grep, sed, pipes and redirection all work; QUOTE Windows paths or write them with forward slashes, an unquoted C:\dir\file loses its backslashes). The `powershell` tool is still the right one for Windows-native cmdlets, services and the registry. Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Non-zero exit codes are reported. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message. A call still running after 30 seconds is moved to the background automatically (same delivery) — pass a timeout long enough for the work; it still applies to a backgrounded call.
tools.name: bash
tools.summary: Execute a child process or shell command

tools.description: Read the contents of a text file (relative or absolute path). Output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files and continue with offset when truncated. To summarise, analyse or review a file rather than work on its text, do not read it here: pass its path to the subagent tool instead.
tools.name: read
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it exists. Use for new files or full rewrites.
tools.name: write
tools.summary: Write a file

tools.description: Fetch a URL over HTTP(S) and return its body as plain text (HTML converted to text, capped at 20000 chars). Use for web pages, docs, and JSON APIs.
tools.name: web_fetch
tools.summary: Read information over a network boundary

tools.description: Search files with ripgrep (regex, Rust syntax). Returns structured file:line:text matches in content mode (default) or just matching paths in files mode. Respects .gitignore and skips hidden/binary files by default. A no-match result is NOT an error.
tools.name: grep
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Exact old_string -> new_string replacement in one existing file. The file must have been read (via the read tool) since its last change, and old_string must occur exactly once unless replace_all=true — ambiguity is an error, never a guess. Use write for creating new files; edit only modifies existing ones.
tools.name: edit
tools.summary: Write a file

tools.description: Look at an image file on disk. Give an absolute path. The image is attached to the conversation and you will see it in the next message -- the result of this call is only a confirmation, not the picture.
tools.name: view_image
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Control the Windows desktop: mouse, keyboard, windows, screenshots. Actions: click/doubleclick/rightclick (need x, y) - marker draws a labelled ring WITHOUT clicking, use it to check your aim first - type/paste/settext (need text) - keypress (key) - activate (pid or window title) - launch (path) - windows - status - screenshot (monitor). TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU: (1) a FAILED activate does not stop a later paste, it types into whatever window has focus, so check the result of activate before doing anything else; (2) paste reports how many characters it sent - read that number and do NOT press Enter unless it matches what you meant to send. Coordinates address windows; titles often cannot, because several windows can share one process. Prefer screenshot then marker then click over activate-by-title.
tools.name: pccontrol
tools.summary: Inspect or control the Windows desktop

tools.description: Drive the user's real Chrome browser. Actions: start / stop / status (the relay this tool talks through) - ping (is the extension answering) - tabs (list open tabs) - nav (needs url, optional new_tab) - text (page text, optional css selector) - click (css selector, or x and y) - write_text (type into a field: needs text, optional selector, clear, enter) - scroll (move the page or an element: dy pixels, negative = up, or to top|bottom — when the page is longer than the viewport, scroll before re-shooting, because a second shot without a scroll shows the same pixels) - shot (screenshot the visible viewport — on a vision model the picture is attached to your next message automatically, so you see it without any extra call). A repeat shot that is byte-identical to the previous one says so and is NOT attached again. On a text-only model, read a scrollable panel (e.g. a filter modal) with text + the panel's CSS selector — it returns the panel's full innerText, below-the-fold included, no scrolling and no vision — rather than repeated shots. A connection error when nothing is running is the normal idle state, not a broken page — call action=start and retry. write_text with no selector types into whatever is focused, so click then write_text works on fields with no stable selector.
tools.name: chrome
tools.summary: Inspect or control the user's Chrome session

tools.description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and get their answers back through a checkbox widget. Pass a `questions` list; each question needs a short `label` (its name in the step bar), the `question` text, and `options` (a list of {title, description?}). Options are MULTI-SELECT: any number of them can be correct — include every plausible one. The widget adds a free-text 'Type something' note field to each question automatically. The user can jump between questions and tick/untick options, use Next to advance through the batch, then Submit after every question has an option or note (the full answer state returns), or press 'Chat about this' (whatever they have entered so far returns and they want to discuss first — Esc cancels with no answers). Use this when the next step depends on a human decision: design choices, ambiguous specs, anything where asking beats guessing.
tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.summary: Ask the user a question inside LiteTUI

tools.description:
Generate media with the LOCAL Lite studio apps — no API keys, no cloud, runs on this machine's GPU.
app=image (LiteImage): actions status | generate | models | load_model (file_path) | unload_model | config | cancel. Generation is synchronous — the reply carries the saved file path. Generate params: prompt + any of width/height/steps/guidance/negative_prompt/seed/sampler/scheduler/batch/lora_dir/init_image_path/strength/clip_skip/output_path/save_to_gallery. guidance defaults to 3.5 (the LiteImage UI value for flux1-dev; the raw API default of 7.5 overdrives it) — pass explicitly for other model families.
app=sound (LiteSound): actions status | generate (mode = music|song|sfx|ambient; prompt and/or lyrics; duration seconds) | job (job_id) | jobs | cancel (job_id) | gallery | backends. Generation is ASYNC: generate returns a job_id — poll with action=job until it reports done, then the file path is in the result. Do not spam polls; every few seconds is plenty.
app=model (LiteModeler, prompt-to-3D): actions status | config | generate (prompt) | families — delegated to the `lst` CLI.
image and sound need their app RUNNING (status says). If one is not running, tell the human to open it — do not retry blind. NEVER call LiteImage's HTTP API directly for GPU work: this tool suspends your own LM Studio model first (shared 5090 VRAM) and restores it after; a raw POST would OOM.
VRAM: on generate/load_model actions this tool SUSPENDS your own model in LM Studio, runs the job to completion, then reloads you at the same context config. You will not notice the gap — but your FIRST reply afterwards re-reads the whole conversation (KV cache is gone), so expect a slow first token and say so if the human wonders. Sound generation is therefore handled to completion INSIDE the call — no polling needed when it returns.
tools.name: studio
tools.summary: Inspect or generate with local studio applications

tools.description:
Listen to audio with a LOCAL Qwen2-Audio model — no cloud, runs on this machine's GPU. Gives you ears: describe sounds, transcribe speech, characterize music.
action=status: readiness report (server binary, model files, your seat state) — cheap, never touches the seat; run it first if unsure.
action=file: listen to an existing audio file (needs `path`; any format ffmpeg reads).
action=record: capture `seconds` from the microphone (`device` optional — default is the first Direct Show input; list names with `ffmpeg -f dshow -list_devices 1 -i dummy`).
question: what to ask about the audio (default: describe exactly what is heard). Keep it specific.
Each real listen SUSPENDS your own LM Studio model, runs Qwen2-Audio through a standalone llama-server on port 8090, and restores you at the same context — expect ~2-3 min per call and a slow first token afterwards. Silence is detected up front (peak < -60 dB) and reported WITHOUT any seat swap.
TRUST its descriptions of speech/music content (speech transcription measured word-perfect). DO NOT trust exact numbers it reports: pitch/tempo/frequency are hallucinated — a pure 440Hz sine came back as '120 bpm'. For precise frequency or loudness analysis use ffmpeg instead of asking.
tools.name: listen
tools.summary: Listen to audio with the local Qwen2-Audio model

tools.description:
Read-only ranked search of the existing index snapshot for the configured data root: owned .agents/<Name>/conversations plus read-only .convos archives, validated at refresh. Lookup never builds or scans the fleet. SQLite FTS5 weights user/assistant 10x tool output. Default ONE ROW PER CONVO; messages=true selects individual messages. First line reports last successful refresh UTC or UNKNOWN; snapshots older than 24h warn but remain searchable. Missing/incompatible/wrong-root indexes refuse with the exact explicit refresh command. No-hit means absent from this snapshot, not necessarily absent from live transcripts.
show: indexed snapshot messages, not a live source read.
raw: currently refuses; authoritative current ownership requires fleet enumeration. Refresh does NOT enable raw access.
stats: snapshot counts by role, not live index health.
refresh=true: separate explicit action; launches a detached hidden refresh with a 3600s budget and returns immediately with PID/log path. The requesting agent/operator must monitor the log for success/failure/timeout. No automatic startup refresh or watcher.
tools.name: convo_search
tools.summary: Read index snapshots; explicit refresh writes the data-root index and launches a process.

tools.description: Request compaction of this conversation at the end of the current tool round, then resume. Use when resolved investigation or repetitive tool output can be replaced by a substantially smaller record without losing what is needed to continue. Preserve decisions, constraints, evidence references, ruled-out approaches, unresolved hypotheses and next actions in the handoff; retain decision-rich planning and unfinished investigations when their detail still matters. This is a request, not proof that compaction succeeded. Local LiteTUI backends only. Automatic compaction remains the fallback. Do not call again immediately after waking without useful intervening work.
tools.name: self_compact
tools.summary: Summarize this conversation and preserve its handoff

tools.description: Search for a skill, or load one. The system prompt lists skills BY NAME ONLY. Pass `find` with keywords to get the matching skills and their one-line descriptions; pass `name` to load that skill's full instructions. Read the instructions before following a skill.
tools.name: skill
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Talk to the LiteHarness agent fleet. Actions: whoami — your agent id, name, tier and whether registration succeeded; discover — which agents are online right now; send — message another agent (requires `to` and `body`); check — poll your inbox immediately instead of waiting for the monitor.
tools.name: harness
tools.summary: Inspect or message the LiteHarness fleet

tools.description: Load the schema of a deferred tool so you can call it. Deferred tools are listed BY NAME ONLY in the system prompt (the 'Deferred tools' section) — their full descriptions and parameters are not in your context until you load them here. Query forms: `select:name,name` loads exactly those names; any other text is keywords matched against tool names and descriptions (up to 8 best matches). Every match is returned in full and becomes callable from your next turn on. Do not guess a deferred tool's parameters; load it first.
tools.name: tool_search
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Delegate a self-contained, single-prompt job to a child model that runs independently on the active backend, in parallel with you. Use it whenever a step is prompt -> response with no tools needed: summarise or analyse a file or a long tool result, translate, classify, extract, draft a section, answer a question from given material. The child has NO tools and NO conversation history: everything it needs goes in `prompt` (the instruction) and `files` (paths it reads itself). Canonical call: {"prompt": "Summarise this README in 3 bullets.", "files": ["README.md"], "background": true}. For an explicit Sol child at High reasoning, call {"prompt": "...", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "reasoning_effort": "high", "background": true}; `think=true` is the legacy medium request, not High. Rules: (1) never read a file yourself only to hand its text over, and never paste file or tool output into `prompt` -- pass the path in `files` (the prompt is streamed token by token and a pasted body stalls you for seconds); (2) use background=true and keep working: the call returns a task id at once, the result arrives later as a message tagged [inbox from task], and the full text is in output/tasks/<id>.log (read it with the read tool); (3) leave max_tokens, think, model, reasoning_effort and system unset unless you have a specific reason. Not for: edits, shell commands, anything that needs tools or your conversation context -- do those yourself.
tools.name: subagent
tools.summary: Read information over a network boundary

tools.authority: desktop_control · destructive_irreversible · external_write · network · process_execution · read_only · self_store · workspace_write
tools.description: Launch a full tool-using child asynchronously, or inspect/cancel its operation. Currently supports autonomous Codex parents and Codex headless children in a retained isolated Git worktree from committed HEAD; dirty parent edits are not inherited. Explicit backend/model/workspace/prompt required for spawn. Returns an operation_id, not a completed result. Child results are durably routed to the launching conversation. Local backends, headed launch, explicit shared workspaces and native app-server parents are blocked pending integration. One managed child globally; no managed grandchildren. Existing lightweight subagent is separate. Status/cancel IDs are scoped to this running parent process; durable outcomes remain retained after restart.
tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.summary: Launch a full tool-using child

tools.authority: desktop_control · destructive_irreversible · external_write · network · process_execution · read_only · self_store · workspace_write
tools.description: Explicit bounded ordinary named-worker dispatch for registered owned leaders. Off until small_task_route is configured. No routing inference, fallback or automatic retry. Provide a fresh persistent worker name, visible pane and a clean separate prepared Git worktree. Scope is a handoff contract, NOT sandbox enforcement or merge permission. Actions: dispatch, status, receipt (leader records worker inbox result; never merged/Done). Any configured backend; a local one is accepted only when its exact model is already loaded, and dispatch never loads a model. Idle reuse unsupported.
tools.name: small_task
tools.summary: Dispatch a visible full worker and persist its receipt

tools.description: Run a PowerShell command in the current working directory (via C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.EXE). PREFER THIS OVER bash ON WINDOWS: bash falls through to cmd.exe here, which has no sleep, no grep, no sed, and breaks on input redirection. Native exit codes are preserved exactly; a failing cmdlet reports 1. Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message. A call still running after 30 seconds is moved to the background automatically (same delivery) — pass a timeout long enough for the work; it still applies to a backgrounded call.
tools.name: powershell
tools.summary: Execute a child process or shell command

tools.description: Execute a shell command in the current working directory (bash on Unix; a real bash (C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe) on Windows: sleep, grep, sed, pipes and redirection all work; QUOTE Windows paths or write them with forward slashes, an unquoted C:\dir\file loses its backslashes). The `powershell` tool is still the right one for Windows-native cmdlets, services and the registry. Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Non-zero exit codes are reported. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message. A call still running after 30 seconds is moved to the background automatically (same delivery) — pass a timeout long enough for the work; it still applies to a backgrounded call.
tools.name: bash
tools.summary: Execute a child process or shell command

tools.description: Read the contents of a text file (relative or absolute path). Output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files and continue with offset when truncated. To summarise, analyse or review a file rather than work on its text, do not read it here: pass its path to the subagent tool instead.
tools.name: read
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it exists. Use for new files or full rewrites.
tools.name: write
tools.summary: Write a file

tools.description: Fetch a URL over HTTP(S) and return its body as plain text (HTML converted to text, capped at 20000 chars). Use for web pages, docs, and JSON APIs.
tools.name: web_fetch
tools.summary: Read information over a network boundary

tools.description: Search files with ripgrep (regex, Rust syntax). Returns structured file:line:text matches in content mode (default) or just matching paths in files mode. Respects .gitignore and skips hidden/binary files by default. A no-match result is NOT an error.
tools.name: grep
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Exact old_string -> new_string replacement in one existing file. The file must have been read (via the read tool) since its last change, and old_string must occur exactly once unless replace_all=true — ambiguity is an error, never a guess. Use write for creating new files; edit only modifies existing ones.
tools.name: edit
tools.summary: Write a file

tools.description: Look at an image file on disk. Give an absolute path. The image is attached to the conversation and you will see it in the next message -- the result of this call is only a confirmation, not the picture.
tools.name: view_image
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Control the Windows desktop: mouse, keyboard, windows, screenshots. Actions: click/doubleclick/rightclick (need x, y) - marker draws a labelled ring WITHOUT clicking, use it to check your aim first - type/paste/settext (need text) - keypress (key) - activate (pid or window title) - launch (path) - windows - status - screenshot (monitor). TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU: (1) a FAILED activate does not stop a later paste, it types into whatever window has focus, so check the result of activate before doing anything else; (2) paste reports how many characters it sent - read that number and do NOT press Enter unless it matches what you meant to send. Coordinates address windows; titles often cannot, because several windows can share one process. Prefer screenshot then marker then click over activate-by-title.
tools.name: pccontrol
tools.summary: Inspect or control the Windows desktop

tools.description: Drive the user's real Chrome browser. Actions: start / stop / status (the relay this tool talks through) - ping (is the extension answering) - tabs (list open tabs) - nav (needs url, optional new_tab) - text (page text, optional css selector) - click (css selector, or x and y) - write_text (type into a field: needs text, optional selector, clear, enter) - scroll (move the page or an element: dy pixels, negative = up, or to top|bottom — when the page is longer than the viewport, scroll before re-shooting, because a second shot without a scroll shows the same pixels) - shot (screenshot the visible viewport — on a vision model the picture is attached to your next message automatically, so you see it without any extra call). A repeat shot that is byte-identical to the previous one says so and is NOT attached again. On a text-only model, read a scrollable panel (e.g. a filter modal) with text + the panel's CSS selector — it returns the panel's full innerText, below-the-fold included, no scrolling and no vision — rather than repeated shots. A connection error when nothing is running is the normal idle state, not a broken page — call action=start and retry. write_text with no selector types into whatever is focused, so click then write_text works on fields with no stable selector.
tools.name: chrome
tools.summary: Inspect or control the user's Chrome session

tools.description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and get their answers back through a checkbox widget. Pass a `questions` list; each question needs a short `label` (its name in the step bar), the `question` text, and `options` (a list of {title, description?}). Options are MULTI-SELECT: any number of them can be correct — include every plausible one. The widget adds a free-text 'Type something' note field to each question automatically. The user can jump between questions and tick/untick options, use Next to advance through the batch, then Submit after every question has an option or note (the full answer state returns), or press 'Chat about this' (whatever they have entered so far returns and they want to discuss first — Esc cancels with no answers). Use this when the next step depends on a human decision: design choices, ambiguous specs, anything where asking beats guessing.
tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.summary: Ask the user a question inside LiteTUI

tools.description:
Generate media with the LOCAL Lite studio apps — no API keys, no cloud, runs on this machine's GPU.
app=image (LiteImage): actions status | generate | models | load_model (file_path) | unload_model | config | cancel. Generation is synchronous — the reply carries the saved file path. Generate params: prompt + any of width/height/steps/guidance/negative_prompt/seed/sampler/scheduler/batch/lora_dir/init_image_path/strength/clip_skip/output_path/save_to_gallery. guidance defaults to 3.5 (the LiteImage UI value for flux1-dev; the raw API default of 7.5 overdrives it) — pass explicitly for other model families.
app=sound (LiteSound): actions status | generate (mode = music|song|sfx|ambient; prompt and/or lyrics; duration seconds) | job (job_id) | jobs | cancel (job_id) | gallery | backends. Generation is ASYNC: generate returns a job_id — poll with action=job until it reports done, then the file path is in the result. Do not spam polls; every few seconds is plenty.
app=model (LiteModeler, prompt-to-3D): actions status | config | generate (prompt) | families — delegated to the `lst` CLI.
image and sound need their app RUNNING (status says). If one is not running, tell the human to open it — do not retry blind. NEVER call LiteImage's HTTP API directly for GPU work: this tool suspends your own LM Studio model first (shared 5090 VRAM) and restores it after; a raw POST would OOM.
VRAM: on generate/load_model actions this tool SUSPENDS your own model in LM Studio, runs the job to completion, then reloads you at the same context config. You will not notice the gap — but your FIRST reply afterwards re-reads the whole conversation (KV cache is gone), so expect a slow first token and say so if the human wonders. Sound generation is therefore handled to completion INSIDE the call — no polling needed when it returns.
tools.name: studio
tools.summary: Inspect or generate with local studio applications

tools.description:
Listen to audio with a LOCAL Qwen2-Audio model — no cloud, runs on this machine's GPU. Gives you ears: describe sounds, transcribe speech, characterize music.
action=status: readiness report (server binary, model files, your seat state) — cheap, never touches the seat; run it first if unsure.
action=file: listen to an existing audio file (needs `path`; any format ffmpeg reads).
action=record: capture `seconds` from the microphone (`device` optional — default is the first Direct Show input; list names with `ffmpeg -f dshow -list_devices 1 -i dummy`).
question: what to ask about the audio (default: describe exactly what is heard). Keep it specific.
Each real listen SUSPENDS your own LM Studio model, runs Qwen2-Audio through a standalone llama-server on port 8090, and restores you at the same context — expect ~2-3 min per call and a slow first token afterwards. Silence is detected up front (peak < -60 dB) and reported WITHOUT any seat swap.
TRUST its descriptions of speech/music content (speech transcription measured word-perfect). DO NOT trust exact numbers it reports: pitch/tempo/frequency are hallucinated — a pure 440Hz sine came back as '120 bpm'. For precise frequency or loudness analysis use ffmpeg instead of asking.
tools.name: listen
tools.summary: Listen to audio with the local Qwen2-Audio model

tools.description:
Read-only ranked search of the existing index snapshot for the configured data root: owned .agents/<Name>/conversations plus read-only .convos archives, validated at refresh. Lookup never builds or scans the fleet. SQLite FTS5 weights user/assistant 10x tool output. Default ONE ROW PER CONVO; messages=true selects individual messages. First line reports last successful refresh UTC or UNKNOWN; snapshots older than 24h warn but remain searchable. Missing/incompatible/wrong-root indexes refuse with the exact explicit refresh command. No-hit means absent from this snapshot, not necessarily absent from live transcripts.
show: indexed snapshot messages, not a live source read.
raw: currently refuses; authoritative current ownership requires fleet enumeration. Refresh does NOT enable raw access.
stats: snapshot counts by role, not live index health.
refresh=true: separate explicit action; launches a detached hidden refresh with a 3600s budget and returns immediately with PID/log path. The requesting agent/operator must monitor the log for success/failure/timeout. No automatic startup refresh or watcher.
tools.name: convo_search
tools.summary: Read index snapshots; explicit refresh writes the data-root index and launches a process.

tools.description: Request compaction of this conversation at the end of the current tool round, then resume. Use when resolved investigation or repetitive tool output can be replaced by a substantially smaller record without losing what is needed to continue. Preserve decisions, constraints, evidence references, ruled-out approaches, unresolved hypotheses and next actions in the handoff; retain decision-rich planning and unfinished investigations when their detail still matters. This is a request, not proof that compaction succeeded. Local LiteTUI backends only. Automatic compaction remains the fallback. Do not call again immediately after waking without useful intervening work.
tools.name: self_compact
tools.summary: Summarize this conversation and preserve its handoff

tools.description: Search for a skill, or load one. The system prompt lists skills BY NAME ONLY. Pass `find` with keywords to get the matching skills and their one-line descriptions; pass `name` to load that skill's full instructions. Read the instructions before following a skill.
tools.name: skill
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Talk to the LiteHarness agent fleet. Actions: whoami — your agent id, name, tier and whether registration succeeded; discover — which agents are online right now; send — message another agent (requires `to` and `body`); check — poll your inbox immediately instead of waiting for the monitor.
tools.name: harness
tools.summary: Inspect or message the LiteHarness fleet

tools.description: Load the schema of a deferred tool so you can call it. Deferred tools are listed BY NAME ONLY in the system prompt (the 'Deferred tools' section) — their full descriptions and parameters are not in your context until you load them here. Query forms: `select:name,name` loads exactly those names; any other text is keywords matched against tool names and descriptions (up to 8 best matches). Every match is returned in full and becomes callable from your next turn on. Do not guess a deferred tool's parameters; load it first.
tools.name: tool_search
tools.summary: Read-only local inspection

tools.description: Delegate a self-contained, single-prompt job to a child model that runs independently on the active backend, in parallel with you. Use it whenever a step is prompt -> response with no tools needed: summarise or analyse a file or a long tool result, translate, classify, extract, draft a section, answer a question from given material. The child has NO tools and NO conversation history: everything it needs goes in `prompt` (the instruction) and `files` (paths it reads itself). Canonical call: {"prompt": "Summarise this README in 3 bullets.", "files": ["README.md"], "background": true}. For an explicit Sol child at High reasoning, call {"prompt": "...", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "reasoning_effort": "high", "background": true}; `think=true` is the legacy medium request, not High. Rules: (1) never read a file yourself only to hand its text over, and never paste file or tool output into `prompt` -- pass the path in `files` (the prompt is streamed token by token and a pasted body stalls you for seconds); (2) use background=true and keep working: the call returns a task id at once, the result arrives later as a message tagged [inbox from task], and the full text is in output/tasks/<id>.log (read it with the read tool); (3) leave max_tokens, think, model, reasoning_effort and system unset unless you have a specific reason. Not for: edits, shell commands, anything that needs tools or your conversation context -- do those yourself.
tools.name: subagent
tools.summary: Read information over a network boundary
